title: The government borrows more

predict.q: Start: real interest rate **6%**, loanable funds **500** (billion), all borrowed for private investment. The government runs a new budget deficit of 100 and borrows it in this market. What happens?

options.s: The real rate falls, because the government adds money to the economy.
options.fb: Borrowing uses existing saving; it competes with firms for the funds.

options.s: The real rate rises and private investment falls.
options.fb: The real rate rises from 6% to 7% and private investment falls from 500 to 450: crowding out.

options.s: The real rate rises and private investment rises too.
options.fb: Total borrowing rises, but the higher rate makes some private projects unprofitable.

options.s: Nothing changes: government borrowing is a separate market.
options.fb: The government borrows from the same savers as firms.

task: Move the deficit slider to 100 and watch the real rate, total borrowing and private investment.

target.do: Move the deficit slider to 100, then press Check.

takeaway: Government borrowing raises the real rate, and some private investment is priced out.
